content: Spouses sought judicial division of a property purchased under legal community; the court assessed “convenient divisibility” and adopted a Court‑Appointed Expert’s plan creating two independent lots (A/B) with a modest equalization. The interpretive problem was whether assignment of the marital home blocks division and how to allocate lots when parties disagree. The judge held that assignment of the home does not prevent division; the right of habitation is opposable to third parties for a limited time but does not bar co‑ownership dissolution. Principles: division favors independent enjoyment with limited depreciation; drawing lots is indicative, not binding—the court may directly assign considering household needs. Counterclaims (fruits, reimbursements) were rejected for generic pleading or legal inapplicability. Costs compensated. 1.
